title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 2, 2026
headline: Gardner Minshew is now ARI's starting QB over Jacoby Brissett. Jeremiyah Love has a new ankle injury, Kendrick Bourne may be done for the season, and Bam Knight is in the concussion protocol.
summary: LaFleur confirmed Gardner Minshew as the starter after the sparks he provided in relief at Dallas. Jacoby Brissett moves to emergency third QB, and Carson (not on the supplied roster) becomes the backup. LaFleur took collective blame for the offense's slow start, especially the run game, and said he sees bad execution as bad coaching. He praised Minshew's pocket movement, accuracy and reads, and said the run game's explosive plays are what loosened the defense. Michael Wilson played through two broken ribs and will be managed through pain; LaFleur said Wilson wants to practice even at 60%. Jeremiyah Love has a new ankle injury (a different part of the ankle than before), and LaFleur will give an update Wednesday. Kendrick Bourne's outlook is not good and might be season-ending. Bam Knight is in the concussion protocol, and LaFleur said he'd know more on Wednesday about Jaden. LaFleur said the receiver and running back plans will look different this week because of the injuries, and Devin Duvernay could be used more. The team is 3-5, preparing for Seattle, and the players got Monday off.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 9 Media Availability | Monday, November 2nd | Press Conference
headline: WR/returner Zachariah Branch (hamstring) and edge Samson Ebukam (hamstring) are out for the Week 9 game against Cincinnati in Madrid; Stefanski stood behind QB Michael Penix Jr. after a sloppy, weather-affected loss to Tampa Bay.
summary: Stefanski opened by saying Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch both have hamstring injuries that will keep them out of this game. He is unsure how long the injuries will last beyond that and said the team will treat them and see how they go over the next couple of weeks. He was disappointed and frustrated by the loss to Tampa Bay. He said both teams faced the same conditions and Atlanta did not do a good enough job, and he credited the Buccaneers. Asked about Penix's interceptions, he said Penix has taken care of the ball well this season, can and will play better, and that the conditions were tough. On the run defense, he did not endorse the idea that one young linebacker was to blame and said the whole unit shares it. He agreed missed tackles were a problem, said tackling is a focus this week, and called the footing a factor but not an excuse. He expressed full confidence in the team's kicker, who has had a rough season, and said he would not think twice about sending him out. Asked about the role of a player returning this week (James Pierce), he said it is too early to say and that a plan will be built over the week. The team now turns to a Week 9 trip to Spain to face Cincinnati.

title: Joe Brady Evaluates Victory Over Baltimore Ravens And Development On Bills Defense
headline: Bills' safety job is open to competition with C.J. Gardner-Johnson back, and Damar Hamlin was steady; Rousseau and Ed Oliver lead a rising defensive front.
summary: Brady had no injury updates because the Bills now hold the medical evaluations after the morning meetings, so MRI results were not in yet. He praised the defense for elite communication and fundamentals in the win over Baltimore, which was played mostly with a backup quarterback after Lamar Jackson left. He said the result was not a product of the opponent's quarterback and came from how the team practiced. Brady singled out Greg Rousseau as a pro who is winning on the edge and affecting the quarterback, helped by Bradley Chubb, T.J. Parker, Deone Walker and Ed Oliver's return. He called Oliver critical to the organization and was happy to see him play free again. On the safety spot, he said Damar Hamlin was as consistent as can be, but he will evaluate the tape with the coordinators and have more answers Wednesday now that C.J. Gardner-Johnson is back. He stressed a culture of competition where players must earn their snaps each week, and he praised a practice-squad call-up who got a game ball. He defended the end-of-half clock management and the aggressive fourth-down approach, though he said there were too many fourth downs because the offense was not good enough on third down. He was also unhappy with 10 penalties, especially pre-snap ones.

Brady said the team did not care who played quarterback for Baltimore, and he does not think the result came from facing a backup. The defense made adjustments as different quarterbacks played.
Jim Leonhard called the game from the press box. Brady called the communication from upstairs to downstairs elite and said the box position makes things a little easier.

The Bills had 10 penalties, including illegal formations, offsides and a delay of game for celebrating. Brady called pre-snap penalties unacceptable but said he does not want to be the league's least-penalized team.

topics.topic: Winning the toss and fourth downs
topics.detail: Brady chose to receive to open and get an early lead, and said it may change with the weather. Fourth-down decisions depend on percentages and game flow, and there were too many because of third-down struggles.

On third-and-25 with no timeouts, the Bills ran the clock down so the defense would play its end-of-half look, then ran a Josh Allen sweep to get in field goal range. Brady said he might have taken two more seconds off the clock but liked the process.

Brady said the defense communicated clearly, and the player making the call owns it, with others trusting it. He praised the secondary for handling a heavy game plan with motions, shifts and zero blitzes.

He said the offensive line is still under discussion and he won't detail changes, though he did open Brady Christensen's 21-day practice window, calling him healthy and fit but in need of football reps. Windows for Xavier Legette and Jonathon Brooks are still being evaluated, and he wants to see more from both on the field before deciding. Jaelan Phillips is day-to-day after hitting good speeds, but with a recurrence in the same area Canales wants him ready for a normal workload, not a limited one. Will Lee III is also day-to-day and trending in the right direction, with the full injury report due Wednesday. Marco Wilson will be out there this week, and Canales praised his movement and aggressiveness despite an emotional roughing penalty. Canales said he wants to fix pass-game protection and rhythm and get back to a balanced run/play-action offense, and he wants to turn takeaways into points. The team is 3-4 and atop the division, and Denver is the next opponent.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference: November 2nd, 2026
headline: Browns (5-3) were routed by Pittsburgh after eight sacks and a stalled run game; Monken says no new injuries, praises Harold Fannin Jr.'s growth, and stays patient with Jared Verse and Denzel Boston as the team heads to New Orleans.
summary: Monken spent the day-after session blaming the loss on the team collectively (coaching, scheme, protection and execution) rather than on any one player, saying that falling behind early forced a drop-back game and produced eight sacks. He said the run game never found a rhythm, with a longest run of seven yards, and that opponents' explosive trap plays also hurt the defense, including a 51-yard gain and a 23-yard pair of plays before halftime. He defended rookie left tackle Spencer Fano as playing his eighth game at a tough position, and said the line is not pleased with where it is but he did not announce any shuffling. He said it is too early to judge Jared Verse, who is still adapting to Cleveland's style and whose sacks should come once the Browns play with the lead. He described Harold Fannin Jr. as an improving player with good hands and run-after-catch ability and said the team should get him the ball more. He said Denzel Boston's heel issue is behind him and that his lack of production is a mix of timing, coverage and missed throws. On health, he said nothing concerning came out of the game and that Carson Schwesinger's ankle has not affected his play. He also said the team lacked poise, with three extracurricular penalties, and is focused on a bounce-back at New Orleans.

Pittsburgh's trap plays produced explosive gains, including a 51-yard run and two trap plays for 23 yards before halftime, and Monken said the Browns must change up their fronts, fits and tackling.

He pointed to the run game as an example: 202 yards at Philadelphia, then about 2.2 yards per carry against Arizona, whose good pad level and won blocks he credited. He blamed a blown coverage and a mental error on the two defensive touchdown breakdowns, and said tackling needs to improve. He said he did not think the offense was too conservative late. He explained that CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens come off the field in certain personnel packages. He saw no disconnect with Dak Prescott over aggressiveness and said they meet weekly. The bright spots were pass rush and Quinnen Williams, who he said played outstanding. Rashan Gary was pulled after his costly penalty, though he still played 11 of the next 19 snaps. On injuries, Downs and Locke are in the protocol, Ferguson and Porter have ankle issues, and Lawrence's ankle could keep him out a few weeks. Jalen Thompson's return will be gauged this week. Schottenheimer said his focus is Indianapolis and dodged questions about the trade deadline.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s defensive depth: ‘[It’s] been significant for us’
headline: Sean Payton wants Jaylen Waddle's role to keep growing, called the run game fixable, and shut down trade-deadline running back rumors.
summary: Payton said the team has extra time off today before the bye, with players coming in only for a lift and film. He said focus comes from building the roster with the right kind of players, and he did not treat the bye as a special challenge. He admitted the ground game is still a work in progress. He saw some glimpses against the Texans, but said some runs could have been blocked better, and he expects improvement. He dismissed the league-leading defensive snap count as a stat he dislikes, and said the offense needs to possess the ball better. On Bo Nix's batted balls, he blamed a mix of good defensive line play, protection issues and technique issues that put defenders in the quarterback's face. He called the young drafted defensive backs getting more playing time significant for the team. He refused to discuss trade rumors, including interest in Jonathan Taylor, and called them internet gossip. He praised Jaylen Waddle as dynamic and quick and said the team needs his plays down the stretch. He noted that Waddle missing practice Wednesday last week made game planning more uncertain.

title: HC Sean Payton on victory over Chiefs: ‘I’m proud of just the grit’
headline: Broncos beat the Chiefs 28-24 on a fourth-quarter rally. Jonah Coleman got open for a big catch-and-run on a play-action shot, and Bo Nix read the blitz.
summary: Sean Payton said he was proud of the team's grit in the 28-24 win over Kansas City, which he called a fourth-quarter game with many ebbs and flows. He said the late defensive stand wasn't a true goal-line defense. A Chiefs false start that pushed them from the 1 back to the 6 was the real swing, and he credited the crowd for it. He said the win was his 200th as a head coach, and that he hates losing more than he likes winning. He used the loss on Monday night 48 days ago as motivation, writing 48 on the grease board. He explained that the offense went for it on fourth-and-2 because it felt it had enough plays, and that it used several plays it had prepared in recent weeks. He admitted the offense struggled in the third quarter, with booing from the crowd after a failed third down. He said he made better calls and hit more runs in the fourth, and that pressure was a cat-and-mouse game with the Chiefs' defense. He described a blitz-beating slipper-boot play where Bo Nix recognized the pressure right away and no defender covered Jonah Coleman, which set up a quick score. He also said the Broncos liked the whole running back draft class and that those backs will play a long time.

title: Sean McVay, Trent McDuffie & Wesley Bailey discuss injury updates, key defensive stops vs. the Chargers, takeaways from Week 8 & more
headline: Rams plan no major receiver trade: Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson will start practice clocks, Davante Adams is still expected back, and Tutu Atwell and Blake Corum are trending up.
summary: McVay opened with injuries. Jaylen Watson re-aggravated his shoulder and will be taken day to day. Trent McDuffie came in better than expected after a knee to the back. Josaiah Stewart hurt a hamstring in warmups and is week to week, and Dean Connors broke his hand, needs surgery and is an IR candidate. Steve Avila felt a little hamstring tightness but should be fine. Myles Garrett will definitely practice this week, and Terrance Ferguson looks more likely than not to start his clock. McVay would not set a ramp-up timeline. He said the team is not expecting to be active at the trade deadline and is counting on getting Garrett, Ferguson, Davante Adams and Kobie Turner back. Poona Ford is the only player lost for the year. On the passing game, McVay said he cares only about winning, noted that the run game has been strong for two weeks, and said Puka Nacua is the main target while the other receivers have had few catches. He praised Tutu Atwell's two plays, said Konata Mumpfield has done well, and said he will use all five eligibles as game flow allows. He credited Blake Corum and Kyren Williams for the run game and said the early-season checkdown volume to the backs dropped because of game script. He was also complimentary of the defensive pressure, Wesley Bailey's growth, and the rookie tight end Max Klare, who he said will see more playing time.

title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Rams
headline: Harbaugh stood pat after the Rams loss: Mike (the offensive coordinator) keeps play-calling, Herbert is not being benched, and he offered no specifics on fixing an offense that has gone nine quarters without a touchdown.
summary: Harbaugh opened by saying the Chargers lost because they could not finish drives with touchdowns, gave up a touchdown late in the first half and one on the Rams' opening drive, and turned the ball over. Pressed on an offense that has gone nine quarters without a touchdown, he said he is aware of it and that the team is the only group that can change it. Asked about Justin Herbert's ten interceptions, he did not address them directly and talked about the team fixing its issues. He said the offense was getting into a rhythm but had three drives that ended without scores, and that the defense played extremely well in the middle eight until turnovers shortened the field. Repeatedly asked why Mike remains the offensive coordinator, he deflected with 'team effort' language and said he would watch the film. He confirmed Mike will continue to call plays, but declined to address anything beyond this game. He flatly rejected the idea of letting Herbert watch from the sideline, and declined to evaluate Herbert's play until he had seen the film. He closed with themes of no quitting, faith in each other, and an opportunity next week. The team is 0-7 and no injury news was given.

signals.claim: Herbert will remain the starting quarterback and will not be benched.
signals.note: Herbert is turning the ball over at a career-high rate (10 INTs), but the coach is not considering a change, so he stays in lineups with a shaky floor.
signals.quote: No.

topics.detail: Harbaugh confirmed Mike will keep calling plays despite the offense's slump and gave no concrete rationale. He said a team-wide fix is needed rather than singling out the coordinator.

The offense has not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, failed to finish three drives with scores, and committed turnovers that gave the Rams short fields. Harbaugh said the defense played extremely well in the middle eight before those turnovers.
At 0-7, Harbaugh emphasized no quit, motivation, dedication, and faith in each other. He said none of the players have been in this position before.

title: Klint Kubiak recaps Week 8: ‘We found a way to win'
headline: Raiders backfield is a three-man committee: Mike Washington Jr. got the bigger workload in the Week 8 win, but Kubiak says Ashton Jeanty and Dylan Laube are still counted on. Jalen Nailor earned more opportunities, and Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and Darien Porter (groin) are being monitored.
summary: Kubiak framed the Week 8 win over the Jets, which snapped a four-game losing streak, as a gritty team victory. He praised Kirk Cousins' calm and his comeback résumé, and Matt Gay's clutch fourth-quarter field goal. On the backfield, he said Mike Washington Jr. ran well and gave the run game a spark, but stressed it was a group effort. He said the Raiders will count on Washington, Ashton Jeanty and Dylan Laube going forward, and that the split is a moving target based on who is playing best. Jeanty was praised for his pass-game plays and protection even though his carries dropped. Jalen Nailor was said to be deserving of more opportunities after his first touchdown catch. Jack Bech's return brought toughness to the run game. The run defense struggled in the first half and is a work in progress. Darien Porter has a groin injury and Tonka Hemingway a stinger, and both are being evaluated. The secondary will keep rotating Jermod McCoy, Darien Porter and Eric Stokes. Trey Zuhn started at right guard and played well, and Kubiak said he believes he will keep getting opportunities.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Nov 1 | Postgame Press Conference
headline: Dolphins blew a big halftime lead in a 24-19 loss to New England. Hafley gave no fantasy-relevant role or injury news beyond a player being medically cleared, and he praised Malik Willis's leadership.
summary: Hafley credited the Patriots as a well-coached team and called the first half possibly Miami's best of the season, with a big lead at the break. He blamed the collapse on missed opportunities and on his young team not yet knowing how to put away a good opponent, and he said he must use the game as a teaching moment. He said the Dolphins did not use the weather as an excuse. He liked the defensive game plan and the three first-half sacks, but said Miami missed chances for more, including a possible sack-fumble. He praised Drake Maye as one of the league's better quarterbacks for extending plays with his feet, hitting a post ball and a roughly 50-yard comeback, and protecting the ball. He declined to discuss the private conversation with young player Ollie about a second-half penalty, saying he needs to teach him how to react in those situations. He praised Malik Willis for telling the young player the truth on the sideline, calling it good leadership. He also said a player referred to as 'Juju' hit all the stages and was medically cleared to play. He ended on a positive note: the team stopped New England late, scored, and got an onside kick chance, which showed resiliency.

injuries.detail: Hafley said the player hit all the stages of his progression, was cleared by the medical staff and was ready to go. It was not a close call.

signals.note: The coach publicly backed Willis's leadership, which signals confidence in him as the locker-room leader at QB.
signals.quote: I think it's good leadership.

signals.claim: Hafley will keep working with him on how to react in tough situations after a second-half penalty.
signals.note: The penalty and Hafley's talk of teaching him composure are a minor discipline flag, with no stated change to his role.
signals.quote: Always a young player who has a lot of fire to him.

topics.detail: Miami led big at halftime but gave up momentum swings after a fourth-down stop was followed by a fourth-down conversion for New England. Hafley called it a lesson in closing out games and said the coaches must coach it better.

Three sacks came in the first half, and the defensive game plan disguised pressures well. Hafley said Miami had near-misses later, including a possible sack-fumble, but could not capitalize in the second half.
Hafley said Maye was unfazed, extended plays with his feet, and hit a post ball and a roughly 50-yard comeback after breaking a sack. He added that Maye took care of the football.
Hafley said weather played no role and he refuses to make excuses about it.
Miami stopped New England in four-minute mode and scored late to earn an onside kick attempt. Hafley saw this as evidence of resiliency that the team must carry across all four quarters.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Injuries Heading into Week 9, Kyler Murray’s Play Action & Overcoming First Loss
headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring), Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) and Theo Jackson (quad) are all sore and being evaluated before Monday night vs. BUF. O'Connell says Murray is still the starter if healthy, and getting Justin Jefferson more touches remains a priority.
summary: O'Connell was disappointed after the first loss of the season to the Lions. He said the team didn't play its best, committed self-inflicted penalties and turnovers, and had too many third-and-7-plus situations. Three players are being evaluated: Kyler Murray's hamstring is sore, Christian Darrisaw has shoulder soreness, and Theo Jackson has a sore quad. O'Connell doesn't think Murray's availability is in jeopardy yet and will update after talking to the medical staff, but he confirmed Murray remains the starter if he is healthy. He said the staff saw chances to get Justin Jefferson the ball more, including misses, play-pass options they didn't pull the trigger on, and protection issues. The Lions often doubled Jefferson on passing downs, so other players like T.J. Hockenson have to punish that coverage. The run game was hurt by a holding call that wiped out the longest run, and the offense ran only about 50 snaps, but he wants to stay committed to the run while building a better balance with the pass. He praised the late pitch-and-catch with Jordan Addison and the Hockenson play as the kind of response the team needs. The team will start on Buffalo with meetings and a walk-through Wednesday, then three practice days before Monday night.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel on being down at halftime 11/1: "It was a good opportunity for us to not be frontrunners"
headline: Patriots beat Miami without Hunter Henry and a depleted WR group; Drake Maye carried the offense, Rhamondre Stevenson praised, Henry's absence noted but no injury details given.
summary: Vrabel framed the Week 8 road win over Miami as a good chance for his team to show it can come from behind and not just play as frontrunners. He said the team started fine but failed to finish drives, missed a field goal, and the defense allowed long drives and conversions to a young, tough Dolphins team. The offense adjusted at halftime and got connected, helped by a Byard interception that turned into points and a defense that handled a sudden-change situation well. Vrabel said the team missed Hunter Henry's leadership and playmaking in close games after he went down, but he praised the offensive staff for moving players around and keeping others ready. He lauded Drake Maye for picking up loose balls, controlling the offense, and winning without his top three receivers or top tight end, and singled out his third quarter and his connection with Jared Wilson. He was complimentary of a Kyle Williams big play and said the run game was decent but occasionally leaky, with no plan yet for next week. He also said the offensive line rotation involving Ben Brown's snaps was decided at halftime. Finally, he spoke warmly of Rhamondre Stevenson reaching 4,000 career rushing yards, citing his preparation, pass protection, and effort, while noting high expectations for him.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 11/2: "I've got a lot of confidence in what Drake does"
headline: A.J. Brown's practice status is uncertain and Hunter Henry (left the game early) has no timetable, while Rhamondre Stevenson earned praise as a do-everything back.
summary: Vrabel was non-committal on A.J. Brown, saying the team will see how he progresses with treatment and what he looks like on Wednesday. He said a group of injured players, including one named by a reporter that sounded like Gilliam, could potentially return this week, but roster-spot moves complicate things. He explained that Ben Brown was put in at halftime over Walter Rouse partly because Brown had worked back from a knee injury, and that they will see how it goes this week. On the passing game, he praised Drake Maye's decision-making and said checkdowns are fine, but the offense needs to play with better flow and not expect big plays on every snap. Hunter Henry did not finish the game and Vrabel has no expectation yet for his return. He expressed confidence in kicker Andy (Borregales) despite misses and gave no hint of a kicker competition. He praised Rhamondre Stevenson for pass protection, catching, tough running and the team-first attitude he showed on the onside kick. He also discussed DeMario Douglas needing to trust his speed after a fumble a couple of weeks ago, and Corey Durden's energy and pad-level coaching points.

title: Kellen Moore on changes coming out of bye week | Saints vs. Browns 2026 NFL Week 9
headline: Saints fired run game coordinator TJ Yates after the bye. Moore is vowing run game and run defense fixes. IR trio (Tyson, Kelvin Banks, Travis Etienne) may start practicing Wednesday, Carlson's job is in question, and Moore praised Kool-Aid McKinstry and Tyler Shough.
summary: Moore opened by detailing bye-week moves: a practice squad swap and the dismissal of run game coordinator TJ, which he framed as a workflow change rather than a knock on a coach he praised. Nugent will now lead the run game structure and the offensive line room, and Moore put the blame for inconsistent rushing on himself, citing play calling, sequencing, fundamentals and scheme. He said the run game was good in New York about three weeks ago but regressed against Pittsburgh, and he promised similar adjustments to run defense, which needs better interior line control, edge contain and finishing at the second and third levels. On injuries, the IR group (Jordan Tyson, Kelvin Banks, Travis Etienne) will work with the training room Monday, and the team will decide whether to open their practice windows Wednesday. Moore said Tyson's timeline is not necessarily beyond expectations and he has had no setback. Kicker Daniel Carlson is under evaluation after field goal struggles, with kicking sessions this week and no commitment to him. Moore was upbeat on the pass defense, singling out Kool-Aid McKinstry and Martin Emerson, and said Tyler Shough played a good game against Pittsburgh. He expects everyone from the Paris game to be part of the week, with two players in concussion protocol. He also downplayed the trade deadline and focused on beating Cleveland.

injuries.detail: On IR and progressing pretty well. Team will decide after Monday's training room work whether to open his practice window Wednesday.

title: Coach John Harbaugh addresses the media after the bye week
headline: Cam Skattebo and Abdul Carter are both day to day heading into the Eagles game, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on IR, so the Giants backfield is thin.
summary: Harbaugh opened by saying the team is getting ready for its division rival, the Eagles, after the bye. Asked about Cam Skattebo and Abdul Carter, he said both are probably day to day up to game time and that he should know more toward the end of the week. He clarified that Carter missed practice because he was sick. He called Tyrone Tracy Jr. a tougher case than Skattebo, and after a reporter pointed it out, he acknowledged Tracy is on IR and won't play. He described the condensed week: an 'act' practice Monday, a practice Tuesday, a mental practice and walkthrough Wednesday, and possibly a Thursday morning walkthrough, which leaves about three days of prep. He said he wasn't busy with trade deadline calls because GM Joe is handling most of them. He confirmed leaving a message for the Titans owner and said the Giants are open to any call and are turning over every stone. He also said the team lacks draft capital, so any addition has to fit a need and the budget, and ideally help both now and later. Locker room chemistry matters in any deal, and he would likely consult players first. He ended with brief remarks about the Ravens and Lamar Jackson's injury, then said the focus is on the next opportunity.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (11/2) | Week 9
headline: Aaron Glenn shut down Breece Hall trade talk, saying 'Breece will still be here,' after Braelon Allen's recent emergence; injury update is deferred until later in the week.
summary: Glenn opened by saying he will give injury updates later in the week. He was disappointed in the outcome of a high-scoring loss. He praised the offense for moving the ball and creating explosive plays, but criticized the 2-of-6 red zone efficiency. He blamed the loss mainly on third-down defensive penalties that gave the opponent second chances, and said the team needs complementary football. Asked about Breece Hall trade speculation, he said Hall is one of the team's better players, the team is in the business of keeping good players, and Hall will remain a Jet. He defended the two early field goal decisions (both fourth-and-three) and said they did not cost the team the game, though next week's approach could differ. On a Brock Bowers touchdown, he said Jarvis Brownlee had good outside leverage but the defense has to make those plays. He said the team is close to getting over the hump in close games, acknowledged it is a bottom-line business, and said nine games remain.

signals.claim: Breece Hall will not be traded and will remain on the Jets roster
signals.note: Removes immediate trade risk, so Hall's role and volume with the Jets stay intact in the short term.
signals.quote: Breece is still a part of this team.

signals.note: Glenn defended Brownlee's coverage on Brock Bowers' touchdown, though the defense still gave up the score; this is relevant for opposing-TE matchups.
signals.quote: Jarvis had great outside leverage.

topics.detail: The Jets went 2-for-6 in the red zone. Glenn called it an ongoing area of work and a key margin in close games.
Third-down penalties extended opposing drives. Glenn pointed to technique fixes and said the defense held the opponent to 2.9 yards per rush but struggled in the passing game.
Glenn stood by kicking field goals on two early fourth-and-three situations and said they did not decide the game, adding next week could be approached differently.

Glenn said the Jets have lost close games, that the team needs to develop a killer instinct, and that he is focused on improving each week rather than on his job security. He added that wins need to come soon, with nine games left.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 2, 2026
headline: Sirianni says no changes to the offensive staff or play caller, and Tanner McKee remains the starting QB. The offense is still struggling, with no specifics on what will change.
summary: Sirianni said he is making no changes to the offensive coaching staff or play-calling, and he put the blame on himself and coordinator Sean for the offense's struggles. He said Tanner McKee is "our guy" and a QB change is not being considered. He said everything is on the table in scheme, practice schedule and play calling, and that unspecified changes have been made behind the scenes. He declined to give McKee's evaluation any injury-based leniency, saying the staff has to find answers whoever is playing. He defended OL coach Chris Kuper as working hard daily, and said the whole operation has to improve rather than any one unit. On a free-rusher sack, he said a pre-snap check left the group not on the same page, and he said it was not Landon Dickerson's fault. He said the defense battled against Washington despite giving up a late 33-yard run. He characterized the run defense as sound on fundamentals apart from the final drive. He gave no injury updates.

signals.claim: McKee will remain the starting QB, with no change planned.
signals.note: McKee's job looks safe for now, but the offense around him is struggling and his ceiling is limited.

topics.detail: Sirianni said no changes will be made to the offensive staff or the play caller. He framed the offense's struggles as a collective coaching and execution problem and took responsibility himself. He said the staff is looking at scheme, practice schedule and play calling, and that unspecified changes have already happened behind the scenes.

A free-rusher sack came after a pre-snap check when the line was not on the same page, which Sirianni called a communication issue involving getting the play in and getting to the line in time. He defended OL coach Chris Kuper as working hard daily and giving players good tools.

Sirianni said the defense battled, since the game was 13-10 for a long stretch. He blamed the late 33-yard run on the game situation after his fourth-and-26 attempt. He pointed to alignment, assignment and block destruction as the keys.

Sirianni said the team is working both within and outside its base system to find what fits its personnel and what it can execute at a high level. He did not describe the system as a source of growing pains.

He praised Rueben Bain for playing physically and in the backfield, like the player Tampa Bay drafted. He said TE Bauer Sharp is coming along, is one of the team's best athletes at the position, and is getting more snaps because he is learning the scheme and blocking willingly. Graham Barton played through an illness, taking IVs and medication, and Bowles said the staff monitored him every time he left the field. Antoine Winfield Jr. played well in his first game back from injury, being physical against the run and getting people lined up. Bowles said the last two games' weather and game scripts meant the Bucs barely threw, but he is very confident in the passing game and said Baker Mayfield had a great week of practice. On injuries, the long-term absentees (Jalen and another player named Josh) will not return to practice this week, and Emeka Egbuka was about 50-50 last week with his status depending on how he progresses. Bowles also said the team now feels like everyone is on the same page and buying in, and he played down concerns about the Raymond James field.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cam Ward finally had a productive game and Tony Pollard is rolling, but the Titans enter their bye with no injury updates until next Wednesday. Amani Hooker is playing at a Pro Bowl level, and Gunnar Helm and the young tight ends are staying involved.

He was frustrated by late-game miscommunication (a snap issue and a Ward/Elic Ayomanor timing problem on the final fourth down) and by repeated drops, including from the veteran receivers. Pollard's recent uptick was credited mostly to Pollard breaking tackles, plus some blocking-scheme and combination changes, especially in the subpackage. He said Amani Hooker, with five interceptions, could break the season record for a safety, and he praised Jacob Martin. Gunnar Helm and the young tight ends will stay involved, Calvin Ridley and Wan'Dale Robinson were told to deliver more, and Jermaine Johnson II is playing through a significant back injury at about 75%. title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/02/26
headline: Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks stepped into bigger receiver roles with Terry McLaurin out, and Dan Quinn said Burks' role keeps growing. Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw were also out.
summary: Quinn was pleased with Washington's win over Philadelphia after a slow start, calling it three good quarters out of four. He was frustrated by the penalties (seven in the first half), a fumble, a drop and a missed field goal, and said the offense must turn field goals into touchdowns. He praised Jayden Daniels' poise, his deep-ball location, and his toughness in coming back after a hard shot late in the first half. With McLaurin out, Quinn highlighted rookie Antonio Williams, who he said was never overwhelmed by the moment, and Treylon Burks, who made a big double-move play and whose role is growing. The defense improved on third down and the line rushed in better coordination for four sacks. Charles Omenihu and Dorance Armstrong Jr. were singled out. Daron Payne was lost to a non-contact injury on Friday and Javon Kinlaw was not expected back, so others stepped up inside. Special teams, including Luke McCaffrey's returns, gave the team a spark.
